objective: Add a code-backed metadata-only Cloud Compute tenant/cell guardrail for VM, Kubernetes, and function workload identity, strong runtime isolation, Kubernetes private/restricted/scheduling posture, and non-secret audit/scheduling/identity evidence refs; reconcile the cloud-k8s manifest and compute registry catalogs to truthful local-foundation claims only.

best_practice_sources.name: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards
best_practice_sources.takeaway: The Restricted profile is aimed at current pod hardening best practices and lower-trust users; this slice requires restricted pod-security posture metadata but does not apply admission policy.

best_practice_sources.name: Kubernetes Service Accounts
best_practice_sources.takeaway: Service accounts provide distinct non-human identities bound to namespaces; this slice requires tenant/cell-scoped service-account refs without creating Kubernetes objects.

best_practice_sources.name: Kubernetes RuntimeClass
best_practice_sources.takeaway: RuntimeClass can select runtime configurations to trade performance for stronger isolation such as hardware virtualization; this slice models allowed isolation labels without configuring CRI handlers.

best_practice_sources.name: Kubernetes Pod Topology Spread Constraints
best_practice_sources.takeaway: Topology spread constraints control placement across failure domains for availability and resource use; this slice requires scheduling evidence refs but does not schedule pods.

best_practice_sources.name: Kubernetes Auditing
best_practice_sources.takeaway: Kubernetes auditing creates security-relevant chronological records for API activity; this slice requires audit evidence refs but does not configure audit backends.

best_practice_sources.name: AWS Lambda best practices
best_practice_sources.takeaway: Lambda guidance recommends most-restrictive execution-role permissions and careful resource/concurrency limits; this slice models function workload identity and isolation metadata only.

best_practice_sources.name: AWS EC2 Instance Metadata Service IMDSv2
best_practice_sources.takeaway: IMDSv2 uses session tokens and can be required on instances; this slice avoids raw instance credentials and only stores non-secret identity evidence refs.

best_practice_sources.name: OCI instance principals
best_practice_sources.takeaway: OCI instance principals let instances call OCI services without user credentials, while access to the instance inherits granted privileges; this slice requires role/identity metadata without OCI calls.

best_practice_sources.name: OCI Audit overview
best_practice_sources.takeaway: OCI Audit records supported public API calls as log events; this slice requires audit evidence refs but does not emit or retrieve OCI audit logs.

implemented_claims: ComputeTenantCellGuardrail validates tenant, region, primary cell, VM instance id, Kubernetes cluster id, function id, VM IAM role ref, Kubernetes service-account ref, function service-account ref, runtime isolation posture, private/restricted/scheduling booleans, and non-secret audit/scheduling/identity evidence refs.
Guardrail resource ids must match tenant, region, and expected kind labels (instance, k8s, function).

Weak runtime isolation labels SharedHost and HardenedNode are rejected for tenant workloads; HardwareVirtualizedVm, KataMicroVm, FirecrackerMicroVm, GvisorSandbox, and WasmSandbox are accepted metadata labels.
Kubernetes guardrail requires private control plane, restricted pod-security posture, and topology-spread evidence metadata.
Evidence refs reject whitespace/control/query/path-traversal/secret-like strings and require evidence/compute/{audit,scheduling,identity}/ prefixes.
Functions/K8s/VM API crates map the new guardrail errors exhaustively without wildcard masking.

cloud-k8s manifest and compute registry catalogs now claim only implemented domain/API/adapter local-foundation surfaces and retire the non-existent compute-kernel catalog row as compatibility metadata.
explicit_non_claims: No live Kubernetes cluster bootstrap, kubeadm, EKS, OKE, EC2, OCI Compute, Lambda, function execution runtime, CNI, CSI, service mesh, REST server, SDK, worker, OpenTofu plan/apply, provider-live smoke, measured SLO, capacity telemetry, DR, or audit-chain runtime persistence is implemented.
No raw cloud credential, kubeconfig, bearer token, private key, Lambda/EC2/OCI credential, service-account secret, or tenant workload payload is introduced or consumed.
The service-local cloud-k8s OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/proto files remain compatibility scaffolds; root contracts/openapi/cloud/cloud-compute-*-v1.yaml files are the code-tested API evidence for this slice.
This ChangeSet does not make Cloud Compute production-ready and does not make full repo ./bin/oya verify --ci-required green.

alternatives_named: Add a narrow metadata guardrail plus manifest truth-down
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The narrow metadata guardrail locks cross-surface compute invariants without faking live provider or scheduler readiness.
rejected_reasons: Live runtime would touch provider credentials, IaC, networking, IAM, observability, and audit persistence too broadly for this sequential slice.
Manifest-only truth-down would not add code-backed workload identity/isolation/scheduling/audit controls.

findings: Guardrail requires tenant/cell-scoped workload identity and rejects secret-like evidence refs.
No raw credentials, kubeconfigs, bearer tokens, private keys, or workload payloads are introduced.

findings: No runtime scheduling, launch, or function execution path is introduced.
The guardrail stores metadata/evidence refs only and avoids tenant payload processing.
Manifest records explicit non-claims for audit persistence, DR, SLOs, and provider-live operations.
